theoryAdd.text: 2's complement works because an n-bit adder really computes modulo 2^n: the discarded carry is exactly a multiple of 2^n. Storing −N as 2^n − N therefore gives the right answer whenever the true result is in range. The same idea extends to any radix r. The radix complement of an n-digit number N is r^n − N (2's, 10's, 16's), and the diminished radix complement is (r^n − 1) − N (1's, 9's, 15's), found by subtracting each digit from r − 1.

theoryAdd.plainText: Radix complement = r^n − N; diminished radix complement = (r^n − 1) − N, one less

theoryAdd.text:
Worked example 1: subtraction by 10's complement (4 digits)
(a) 7832 - 2456
    10's comp of 2456 = 7544
    7832 + 7544 = 1 5376  -> end carry: result positive = 5376
(b) 2456 - 7832
    10's comp of 7832 = 2168
    2456 + 2168 = 4624    -> no end carry: result negative
    answer = -(10's comp of 4624) = -5376

With the diminished complement (9's or 1's) an end carry is not discarded but added back to the least significant digit, which is the end-around carry. For example, 745 − 283 gives 745 + 716 = 1461, and 461 + 1 = 462. If there is no end carry, the result is negative and its magnitude is the 9's (or 1's) complement of the sum: 283 − 745 gives 283 + 254 = 537, so the answer is −462. The end-around carry is the extra addition that 2's complement avoids.

Worked example 2: (-75) + (-80) in 8 bits
  -75 = 1011 0101
  -80 = 1011 0000
  sum = 1 0110 0101
carry into MSB = 0, carry out of MSB = 1 -> V = 1
result 0110 0101 = +101 (true sum -155 < -128): overflow

; 8086: the same bits compared as signed and unsigned
        MOV  AL, 0F0H    ; -16 signed, 240 unsigned
        MOV  BL, 10H     ; +16
        CMP  AL, BL      ; E0H: CF=0, SF=1, OF=0, ZF=0
        JB   BELOW       ; not taken: CF = 0 (240 > 16)
        JL   LESS        ; taken: SF != OF (-16 < +16)
LESS:   MOV  AL, 9CH     ; -100
        CBW              ; AX = FF9CH, sign copied into AH
BELOW:  HLT

Widening and narrowing follow one rule: the value is unchanged only if the bits added or removed are copies of the sign bit. FF80H can be cut to 80H (both −128), but 0080H cannot, because +128 would become −128. An arithmetic shift right divides by 2 and rounds toward minus infinity, so 1111 1011 (−5) becomes 1111 1101 (−3), not −2.

items: Reporting overflow whenever there is a carry out; in signed arithmetic V = carry into MSB XOR carry out of MSB.
Zero-extending a negative number, e.g. turning 1011 (−5) into 0000 1011 (+11).
Forgetting the end-around carry in 1's or 9's complement, or wrongly adding it in 2's or 10's complement.
Using the 2's complement range −2^(n−1) to 2^(n−1) − 1 for sign-magnitude or 1's complement, which only reach ±(2^(n−1) − 1).
Reading a negative result of complement subtraction directly instead of complementing it to get the magnitude.

theoryAdd.text: After a subtraction, the 8085 CY flag and the 8086 CF flag hold the borrow, which is the complement of the adder's internal carry-out. 5AH − 3CH leaves CY = 0 (no borrow) even though the adder produced a carry of 1.

questions.questionText: The 8-bit sign-magnitude representation of −25 is:
questions.explanation: +25 = 0001 1001; sign-magnitude only sets the sign bit, giving 1001 1001. 1110 0110 and 1110 0111 are the 1's and 2's complement forms.

questions.questionText: The 8-bit 1's complement representation of −37 is:
questions.explanation: +37 = 0010 0101; inverting every bit gives 1101 1010. Adding 1 would give the 2's complement 1101 1011, and 1010 0101 is sign-magnitude.

questions.questionText: The range of a 6-bit 2's complement number is:
questions.explanation: An n-bit 2's complement number covers −2^(n−1) to 2^(n−1) − 1: −2⁵ = −32 to 2⁵ − 1 = +31. −31 to +31 is the 1's complement range; 0 to 63 is unsigned.

questions.questionText: The range of an 8-bit sign-magnitude number is:
questions.explanation: Seven bits hold the magnitude (0 to 127) and one bit the sign, so the range is ±(2⁷ − 1) = −127 to +127, with two codes for zero.

questions.questionText: Which signed-number representation has only one code for zero?
questions.explanation: Sign-magnitude has +0 and −0 (0000 and 1000) and 1's complement has 0000 and 1111; in 2's complement negating 0000 gives 0000 again, so there is a single zero.

questions.questionText: The 9's complement of the decimal number 3528 is:
questions.explanation: Subtract each digit from 9: 9999 − 3528 = 6471. Adding 1 would give the 10's complement 6472.

questions.questionText: The 10's complement of the 4-digit decimal number 4700 is:
questions.explanation: 10's complement = 10⁴ − 4700 = 5300 (or 9's complement 5299 + 1). The trailing zeros stay zero.

questions.questionText: The 4-bit 2's complement number 1010 is sign-extended to 8 bits. The result is:
questions.explanation: Sign extension copies the sign bit (1) into all new upper positions: 1111 1010, still −6. 0000 1010 would change the value to +10.

questions.questionText: The most negative number that can be stored as a 16-bit 2's complement integer is:
questions.explanation: The range is −2¹⁵ to 2¹⁵ − 1, so the most negative value is −32768 (8000H). −32767 is the limit for 16-bit 1's complement or sign-magnitude.

questions.questionText: The 8-bit 2's complement pattern 1000 0000 represents:
questions.explanation: The MSB has weight −2⁷ and all other bits are 0, so the value is −128. It has no positive partner in 8 bits.

questions.questionText: In 4-bit 1's complement, the two codes that represent zero are:
questions.explanation: Inverting +0 = 0000 gives 1111, which is −0 in 1's complement. 0000 and 1000 are the two zeros of sign-magnitude.

questions.questionText: In 2's complement addition, overflow can never occur when:
questions.explanation: Adding a positive and a negative number gives a result whose magnitude is no larger than the larger operand, so it always fits. A negative result can itself be the sign of overflow when two positives are added.

questions.questionText: The 8-bit 2's complement of 3AH is:
questions.explanation: 100H − 3AH = C6H (or invert 3AH to C5H and add 1). BAH just sets the sign bit, as in sign-magnitude.

questions.questionText: The 4-bit 2's complement number 1101 has the decimal value:
questions.explanation: −8 + 4 + 0 + 1 = −3. Read as unsigned it is 13, as sign-magnitude −5 and as 1's complement −2.

questions.questionText: How many distinct numeric values can an n-bit 1's complement number represent?
questions.explanation: There are 2^n bit patterns, but two of them (all 0s and all 1s) both mean zero, leaving 2^n − 1 distinct values, e.g. 15 for 4 bits (−7 to +7).

questions.questionText: Using 8-bit 2's complement, (+45) + (−20) is computed as 0010 1101 + 1110 1100. The correct result is:
options: 0001 1001 (+25), with the carry out of the MSB discarded
questions.explanation: 0010 1101 + 1110 1100 = 1 0001 1001; discard the carry to get 0001 1001 = +25. The operands have opposite signs, so there is no overflow.

questions.questionText: The 8-bit pattern 1101 0110 is a 2's complement number. Its decimal value is:
questions.explanation: −128 + 64 + 16 + 4 + 2 = −42 (or negate: 0010 1010 = 42). 214 is the unsigned value, −86 the sign-magnitude reading and −41 the 1's complement reading.

questions.questionText: Which of these additions of 8-bit 2's complement numbers produces overflow?
questions.explanation: +150 exceeds the 8-bit limit of +127, so the result wraps to a negative pattern. −120 and −50 are in range; the opposite-sign sums can never overflow.

questions.questionText: Two 8-bit 2's complement numbers 1111 1111 (−1) and 1111 1111 (−1) are added. Which describes the result?
questions.explanation: 1111 1111 + 1111 1111 = 1 1111 1110. The carry-out is 1, but the carry into the MSB is also 1, so V = 1 ⊕ 1 = 0: −2 is correct and the carry is simply discarded.

questions.questionText: In 8-bit 1's complement arithmetic, (+9) + (−4) is computed as 0000 1001 + 1111 1011. The correct result is:
questions.explanation: 0000 1001 + 1111 1011 = 1 0000 0100. In 1's complement the carry is added back to the LSB: 0000 0100 + 1 = 0000 0101 = +5. Discarding it (the 2's complement rule) would give 4.

questions.questionText: 7832 − 2456 is performed by adding the 10's complement of 2456 to 7832 and discarding the end carry. The result is:
questions.explanation: 10's complement of 2456 = 7544; 7832 + 7544 = 15376. The end carry shows the result is positive, so drop it: 5376.

questions.questionText: 745 − 283 is performed using the 9's complement method with end-around carry. The final result is:
questions.explanation: 9's complement of 283 = 716; 745 + 716 = 1461. Add the end-around carry to the remaining digits: 461 + 1 = 462.

questions.questionText: The 8-bit 2's complement value F5H is sign-extended to 16 bits. The result is:
questions.explanation: F5H has its sign bit set (it is −11), so the new upper byte is filled with 1s: FFF5H, still −11. 00F5H would be +245.

questions.questionText: An arithmetic shift right by one place is applied to the 8-bit 2's complement number 1110 1000 (−24). The result is:
questions.explanation: An arithmetic right shift moves every bit right and copies the sign bit into the MSB, giving 1111 0100 = −12 (−24 ÷ 2). A logical shift would insert 0 and give 0111 0100; 1101 0000 is the left shift.

questions.questionText: During an 8-bit 2's complement addition the carry into the sign bit is 1 and the carry out of the sign bit is 0. This means:
options: Overflow: two positive operands produced a negative result
Overflow: two negative operands produced a positive result
No overflow; the carry out is simply discarded
No overflow, but the unsigned result is wrong
questions.explanation: V = Cin(MSB) ⊕ Cout(MSB) = 1 ⊕ 0 = 1, so overflow. A carry-out of 0 with a carry-in of 1 is only possible when both sign bits are 0, and the sign bit of the result then becomes 1.

questions.questionText: Which statement about 8-bit 2's complement is NOT correct?
options: Taking the 2's complement twice returns the original number
questions.explanation: Inverting 1000 0000 gives 0111 1111, and adding 1 gives 1000 0000 again: −128 has no positive partner in 8 bits. The other three statements are true.

questions.questionText: On the 8086, AL = 9CH. After the instruction CBW, register AX contains:
questions.explanation: CBW copies bit 7 of AL into all bits of AH. 9CH has bit 7 = 1 (it is −100), so AH = FFH and AX = FF9CH, still −100.

questions.questionText: The byte FFH is interpreted as an unsigned number and as an 8-bit 2's complement number. Its two values are:
questions.explanation: As unsigned, FFH = 255. In 2's complement, 1111 1111 = −128 + 127 = −1. −127 would be the sign-magnitude reading.

questions.questionText: The minimum number of bits needed to represent −200 in 2's complement is:
questions.explanation: 8 bits cover only −128 to +127. 9 bits cover −256 to +255, which includes −200, so 9 bits are needed.

questions.questionText: An 8-bit adder performs 5AH − 3CH by adding the 2's complement of 3CH. The 8-bit result and the adder's carry-out are:
questions.explanation: 2's complement of 3CH = C4H; 5AH + C4H = 11EH. The 8-bit result is 1EH (90 − 60 = 30), and the carry-out of 1 means no borrow was needed.

questions.questionText: Using an 8-bit adder, 0001 0010 (18) − 0010 1101 (45) is computed by adding the 2's complement of the subtrahend. The result and carry-out are:
questions.explanation: 2's complement of 0010 1101 is 1101 0011; 0001 0010 + 1101 0011 = 1110 0101 with no carry. The pattern is −27 (negate: 0001 1011 = 27). 1110 0100 results from using the 1's complement.

questions.questionText: The 16-bit word FF38H is a 2's complement integer. Its decimal value is:
questions.explanation: Negate: invert FF38H to 00C7H and add 1 to get 00C8H = 200, so the value is −200. 65336 is the unsigned reading and −32568 the sign-magnitude reading.

questions.questionText: The 4-bit 2's complement number 1011 is extended to 8 bits and added to 0000 0111. The 8-bit result is:
questions.explanation: Sign extension gives 1111 1011 (−5); 1111 1011 + 0000 0111 = 1 0000 0010, discard the carry: +2. Zero-extending to 0000 1011 would wrongly add 11 + 7 = 18.

questions.questionText: The 16's complement of the 3-digit hexadecimal number 3AF is:
questions.explanation: 16's complement = 16³ − 3AFH = 1000H − 3AFH = C51H. The 15's complement (subtract each digit from F) is C50, and adding 1 gives C51.

questions.questionText: The 9's complement of the BCD digit 0111 (7) is:
questions.explanation: 9 − 7 = 2, which in BCD is 0010. 1000 is the bitwise (1's) complement of 0111, which is not the 9's complement in BCD.

questions.questionText: A 16-bit 2's complement value is to be truncated to its low 8 bits. For which value does truncation keep the numeric value unchanged?
questions.explanation: FF80H = −128 and its low byte 80H is also −128. 0080H (+128) would become −128, FF7FH (−129) would become +127, and 0100H (+256) would become 0.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a reason why computers use 2's complement for signed integers?
options: It has only one representation of zero
The same adder circuit performs both addition and subtraction
No end-around carry is needed after addition
It gives a symmetric range with equal numbers of positive and negative values
questions.explanation: The 2's complement range is asymmetric, −2^(n−1) to 2^(n−1) − 1, with one more negative value. The other three are genuine advantages over sign-magnitude and 1's complement.

questions.questionText: 2456 − 7832 is performed by adding the 10's complement of 7832 to 2456. No end carry is produced. The correct final result is:
questions.explanation: 10's complement of 7832 = 2168; 2456 + 2168 = 4624 with no end carry, so the answer is negative and equals the 10's complement of 4624: −5376.

questions.questionText: An 8-bit 2's complement unit computes (+100) − (−50). Which statement describes the result bits and the overflow flag V?
questions.explanation: Subtracting −50 means adding +50: 0110 0100 + 0011 0010 = 1001 0110. The true answer +150 exceeds +127, so V = 1 and the pattern reads as −128 + 22 = −106.

questions.questionText: The 8-bit 2's complement numbers −75 (1011 0101) and −80 (1011 0000) are added. The 8-bit result, carry-out C and overflow V are:
questions.explanation: 1011 0101 + 1011 0000 = 1 0110 0101, so C = 1 and the result reads +101. Two negatives produced a positive (true sum −155 < −128), so V = 1: carry into the MSB is 0 and carry out is 1.

questions.questionText: In an 8-bit 2's complement addition the carry out of the MSB is 1 and the carry into the MSB is 0. What can be concluded?
options: Both operands were positive and overflow occurred
The operands had opposite signs and there is no overflow
Both operands were negative, the result is positive, and overflow occurred
Both operands were negative and there is no overflow, because the carry is discarded
questions.explanation: A carry out of the sign position with no carry into it requires both sign bits to be 1, and their sum bit is then 1 + 1 + 0 = 0. V = 1 ⊕ 0 = 1: two negatives gave a positive.

questions.questionText: On the 8086, AL = 80H. After ADD AL, 80H the contents of AL and the flags CF, OF and ZF are:
questions.explanation: 80H + 80H = 100H, so AL = 00H, CF = 1 and ZF = 1. As signed values (−128) + (−128) = −256 is out of range and two negatives gave a non-negative result, so OF = 1.

questions.questionText: On the 8086, AL = 50H. After SUB AL, 70H the contents of AL and the flags CF, OF and SF are:
questions.explanation: 50H − 70H = −20H = E0H. A borrow was needed (50H < 70H), so CF = 1; bit 7 is 1, so SF = 1. As signed values 80 − 112 = −32 is in range, so OF = 0.

questions.questionText: On the 8086, AL = F0H and BL = 10H. The instruction CMP AL, BL is executed. Which conditional jumps would be taken next?
options: JB is taken (unsigned 240 < 16), but JL is not taken
JL is taken (signed −16 < +16), but JB is not taken (unsigned 240 > 16)
Both JL and JB are taken
Neither JL nor JB is taken
questions.explanation: F0H − 10H = E0H with no borrow, so CF = 0 (JB not taken); SF = 1 and OF = 0, so SF ≠ OF and JL (signed less) is taken. The same bits compare differently as signed and unsigned numbers.

questions.questionText: Two 16-bit 2's complement numbers are subtracted: 1234H − 5678H. The 16-bit result and its signed decimal value are:
questions.explanation: 1234H + (2's complement of 5678H = A988H) = BBBCH. It is negative, and negating gives 4444H = 17476, so the value is −17476. BBBBH comes from using the 1's complement; 48060 is the unsigned reading.

questions.questionText: The 8-bit pattern 1011 0101 is read in sign-magnitude, 1's complement and 2's complement, in that order. Its three values are:
questions.explanation: Sign-magnitude: magnitude 011 0101 = 53, so −53. 1's complement: invert to 0100 1010 = 74, so −74. 2's complement: −128 + 53 = −75. As unsigned it would be 181.
